questions.stem: A nightly job starts a thread that adds up the day's sales into a shared map, then calls join() on that thread and writes the map out as a report. Halfway through the rows, the adding-up throws a NullPointerException on a malformed row. What does the job's main thread do, and why?

options.text: join() throws the NullPointerException and no report goes out, since the failure is rethrown in the main thread
options.says: nothing connects a thread's failure to the thread that started it; join() returns normally

options.text: join() throws an ExecutionException and no report goes out, since the failure reaches the main thread wrapped
options.says: ExecutionException comes from Future.get() on a Callable's outcome; join() on a thread that ran a Runnable returns normally

options.text: join() returns normally and the report goes out from a partly filled map, since the failure stays with the thread it happened in
options.says: an uncaught exception ends its own thread and goes to that thread's uncaught-exception handler; join() waits for the thread to end, not for it to succeed

options.text: join() returns normally and the report goes out from a partly filled map, since the failure is held until the main thread asks for it
options.says: a Runnable's failure is not kept for the main thread to ask for: it goes to the failing thread's uncaught-exception handler, whose default prints it

origin.section: A Runnable Has No Way Back: Return a Result or a Failure Through a Callable

questions.stem: A command-line importer starts a daemon thread that writes progress lines to import.log through a BufferedWriter opened in try-with-resources. The main thread finishes the import and returns from main while the daemon thread is still writing, with its last few lines still in the writer's buffer. What ends up in import.log, and why?

options.text: The lines already flushed and none of the buffered ones, since the thread is interrupted and its catch block throws the buffer away
options.says: the daemon thread is not interrupted and gets no exception at exit; it simply stops, so nothing closes or flushes the writer

options.text: The lines already flushed and none of the buffered ones, since the thread is stopped where it stands with no cleanup run
options.says: at exit a daemon thread is dropped mid-step: no exception, no finally, so try-with-resources never closes and flushes the writer

options.text: Every line the thread goes on to write, since the JVM waits for a thread that has a file open
options.says: the JVM waits only for started non-daemon threads; on the page, the daemon exporter had its writer open and the JVM exited anyway

options.text: Every line the thread goes on to write, since a daemon thread finishes its current task before exit
options.says: a daemon thread doesn't hold the JVM open, so its task is abandoned wherever it is when the last non-daemon thread ends

origin.section: A Daemon Thread Doesn't Hold the JVM Open, and Exit Drops It Mid-Step

questions.stem: A small upload tool's main method starts one thread per file with Thread.ofVirtual().start(...) for 30 files, and returns right after starting them, without waiting. No other threads of the tool are running. What happens to the uploads, and why?

options.text: The JVM waits for all 30 uploads, since a thread made this way always takes the daemon status of main
options.says: platform threads inherit daemon status; a virtual thread is always a daemon and can't be made non-daemon

options.text: The JVM waits for all 30 uploads, since a thread made this way always starts out as a non-daemon
options.says: a virtual thread is a daemon by definition, and setDaemon(false) on one throws IllegalArgumentException

options.text: The JVM exits as main returns, and uploads in progress finish first, since a thread made this way always completes its task
options.says: at exit a daemon thread, and every virtual thread is one, is dropped mid-step

options.text: The JVM exits as main returns, and uploads in progress are dropped, since a thread made this way is always a daemon
options.says: virtual threads are always daemon threads; once main ends, no non-daemon thread is left

origin.section: A Virtual Thread Is Cheap to Create and to Block, Not Faster at Computing

questions.stem: A photo service resizes uploads in memory, about 200 ms of pure computation per photo, on a fixed pool of 16 platform threads on a machine with 16 logical CPUs. Someone proposes starting one virtual thread per photo instead. With 400 photos waiting, how does the time to finish them change, and why?

options.text: It stays about the same, since 16 CPUs compute 16 photos at a time
options.says: a virtual thread makes blocking cheap, not computation faster; the CPUs are the limit for CPU-bound work

options.text: It stays about the same, since 16 CPUs allow only 16 virtual threads
options.says: a JVM runs far more virtual threads than it has CPUs (100,000 on the page); the CPUs limit how many compute at a time, not how many exist

options.text: It drops sharply, since 16 CPUs compute 400 virtual threads' photos together
options.says: only as many tasks compute at once as there are CPUs, whatever kind of thread runs them

options.text: It drops sharply, since 16 CPUs schedule virtual threads more cheaply
options.says: computing tasks took the same time on either kind of thread; virtual threads save the cost of blocking, not of arithmetic

origin.section: A Virtual Thread Is Cheap to Create and to Block, Not Faster at Computing
